- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ray Charles testified before Congress in support of copyright reform for recording artists.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In 1979, Ray Charles participated in the Musicians United for Safe Energy concert in support of anti-nuclear activism.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ray Charles was a passionate and committed activist who fought for social justice and equality.
- [USER] User asked if Ray Charles ever faced backlash for his activism and how he handled it.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ray Charles faced backlash for canceling a show in Augusta, Georgia, in 1961 due to the venue's segregation policy, which resulted in negative press and death threats.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ray Charles stood by his decision to cancel the show and continued to speak out against racism and segregation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In a 1962 interview with Jet magazine, Ray Charles stated, "I'm not a crusader, but I am a man who believes in equal rights for all."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Despite criticism and threats, Ray Charles remained committed to his activism until his death in 2004.
